goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Indexing [0]['id'] on the embed_category lookup crashes the migration whenever that setting was never persisted, which is the common case

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:15 — The uncategorized_category_id fallback is unreachable and would itself index [0] on an empty result because that hidden setting is only persisted after seeding
db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — DELETE FROM site_settings destroys the only copy of embeddable_hosts and embed_category even when the backfill inserted nothing
db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:2 — def change contains raw execute calls, so the migration is irreversible and rake db:rollback fails instead of dropping the table

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `def change` but contains multiple raw `execute(...)` calls (data copy and deletes from `site_settings`). In Rails, `execute` has no automatic inverse, so a `change` migration that includes it is treated as irreversible unless wrapped in a `reversible` block or split into explicit `up`/`down`. As a result, `db:rollback` would raise an `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` error rather than cleanly reversing (including dropping the created table).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The raw INSERT bypasses EmbeddableHost normalization and validation, so scheme/path hosts never match record_for_host and embedding silently breaks

Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the migration’s raw INSERT bypasses EmbeddableHost normalization/validation, causing hosts with schemes or paths to not match the lookup method (record_for_host) and thus break embedding—this is the same core issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Site-setting text is interpolated into SQL unescaped, so a host containing a quote aborts the migration or injects SQL

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds an INSERT statement via string interpolation: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` inside `records.each do |h|`. The value `h` comes from the `site_settings` table (previous `embeddable_hosts` setting) and is not SQL-escaped or parameterized. If any stored host contains a single quote, the migration SQL will break and abort; additionally, crafted content could alter the SQL executed during migration. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — create_table with force: true silently drops the table and all its rows if the migration is ever re-applied

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table with that name before recreating it, which would destroy any existing rows instead of raising an error. While migrations normally run once, the behavior described (data loss if the migration is rerun against a DB where the table already exists, e.g., partial/failed runs or manual table creation) is directly implied by the code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25 — Blank category falls back to uncategorized_category_id whose default is -1, writing a nonexistent category into a null: false column with no foreign key

adjudication.rationale: The controller does fall back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when `category_id` is blank, and the migration makes `embeddable_hosts.category_id` `null: false` with no FK. However, the finding hinges on an unproven assumption in this diff: that `uncategorized_category_id` “defaults to -1”. Nothing in the diff shows the default value or that it can be -1 in practice. Even if it were -1, it would not violate the `null: false` constraint (it would just be a potentially invalid reference, and there’s no foreign key here to enforce existence). So the specific claimed defect is not directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:4 — No index or uniqueness constraint on host despite case-insensitive lower(host) lookups and a backfill that can insert duplicates

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `host` non-null but adds no index or uniqueness constraint on `host`. Yet the model does case-insensitive lookups via `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, and `TopicEmbed.import` relies on `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` to select a single category mapping. With duplicates allowed (including from the backfill which inserts raw `h` values via SQL without normalization/validation), the `.first` match is ambiguous and can yield inconsistent category selection, and performance can degrade without an index on `host`/`lower(host)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:16 — Embedding` is a fake `OpenStruct` resource with a hardcoded `id: 'default'` that only wraps `EmbeddableHost.all`, so an index action on the existing embeddable_hosts resource would delete the whole adapter/route/serializer/controller layer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces an `Admin::EmbeddingController` whose `fetch_embedding` builds an `OpenStruct` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` so the admin UI can load a single “embedding” model that contains the list of hosts (via `EmbeddingSerializer has_many :embeddable_hosts`). This is an architectural choice to present a singleton resource; it is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect by itself. The proposed finding is essentially a refactor suggestion (use an index action on `embeddable_hosts` instead), not a concrete problem introduced by the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 — update` renders exactly the same payload as `show` and mutates nothing, making the PUT route at config/routes.rb:139 a dead write endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, ...)` exactly like `show` and does not read params or persist any changes. `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` from `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`, so there is nothing to update on it. Yet routes add `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, and the Ember controller calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, meaning the PUT is effectively a no-op “dead write” endpoint in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5 — The `saveChanges` action is referenced by no template, so it is dead code feeding the no-op server update.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only new admin embedding template (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) invokes actions `addHost` (via the bottom d-button) and `deleteHost` (passed into the `embeddable-host` component). There is no invocation of `saveChanges`, and no other added/modified template shown references it, so within this diff the `saveChanges` action in `admin-embedding.js.es6` is unused. However, this is primarily dead/unused code (and the server `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is effectively a no-op), which is not a clear correctness/behavioral defect introduced by the diff unless there was an intended save UI missing (not verifiable from the diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4 — The `id`, `host`, and `category_id` methods only re-delegate to `object.<same_name>`, which the `attributes` declaration already does.

adjudication.rationale: In app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb the methods `id`, `host`, and `category_id` simply return `object.id`, `object.host`, and `object.category_id`, which ActiveModel::Serializer (and Discourse’s ApplicationSerializer pattern) already provides when those fields are listed in `attributes`. This is redundant, but it does not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect—removing them would not change behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:3 — before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` duplicates the filters inherited from `Admin::AdminController` and the route's `AdminConstraint`, and is repeated in app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:3.

Therefore this is not a real, diff-verifiable problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:200 — The `hydrated || []` fallback is unreachable because `Array#map` on line 197 always returns an array.

adjudication.rationale: In the new plural-IDs branch, `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` will always produce an Array-like object when it runs successfully, which is always truthy; therefore `hydrated || []` is redundant. However, this is not a functional defect—just dead/redundant fallback logic. If `obj[k]` is nil/non-array, the code would throw before reaching the `|| []` anyway, so the finding doesn’t identify a real correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:201 — The new plural branch always runs `delete obj[k]` while the singular branch deletes only on a successful lookup (line 206), an undocumented divergence inside one helper.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `store.js.es6` the new plural hydration branch (`*_ids`) unconditionally deletes the original `obj[k]` (the ids array) after mapping ids through `_lookupSubType`. Unlike the singular `*_id` branch, it does not guard deletion on a successful lookup. If any or all ids cannot be hydrated (e.g., missing from `root`), the code will still remove the original ids list and replace it with an array containing `undefined` entries (since `.map` always returns an array), losing the raw ids data that the singular path preserves when lookup fails. This is a concrete behavioral divergence introduced by the diff and can cause downstream code to lose reference information when hydration fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:9 — categoryId` duplicates `host.category` outside the `bufferedProperty('host')` buffer, requiring manual seeding (line 26) and re-sync via the `Discourse.Category` global (line 38) and escaping `rollbackBuffer()` on cancel (line 58).
app/models/embeddable_host.rb:12 — record_for_host` returns `false` for bad input but a record or `nil` otherwise, giving one finder three return types callers must guess at.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, the method does indeed return `false` for malformed input, and otherwise returns an `EmbeddableHost` record or `nil` (`where(...).first`). However, in this diff all current call sites handle both `false` and `nil` equivalently: `host_allowed?` uses `.present?` (false/nil => false), and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` (false/nil => nil). So while the mixed return types are a mild API/design smell, it does not introduce a verifiable bug/correctness defect in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:153 — resources :embeddable_hosts` generates index/show/new/edit routes the controller never implements, so it should be scoped with `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]`.

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the diff adds `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new`, which by default creates routes for index/show/new/edit in addition to create/update/destroy. The new Admin::EmbeddableHostsController in the diff only defines `create`, `update`, and `destroy` (no `index`, `show`, `new`, `edit`). That means requests like `GET /admin/embeddable_hosts` will route to a missing action and raise `AbstractController::ActionNotFound` (undesired/incorrect routing). Scoping the routes with `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]` would fix the mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_', '-')` normalizes only the first underscore and bolts an ad-hoc naming fixup onto `basePath`, a code path shared by every model.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `basePath(store, type)` now checks `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-')) !== -1)`. While `String#replace` without a global regex only replaces the first underscore, the only values added/used here (`embeddable_host` / `site_customization`) each contain a single underscore, and the `ADMIN_MODELS` entries themselves (`plugin`, `site-customization`, `embeddable-host`) have no multiple-underscore forms. For all other models, this expression doesn’t change behavior because either there is no underscore to replace or the model isn’t in `ADMIN_MODELS` anyway. So the finding points out a potential future/general concern, but it is not a concrete, verifiable bug introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:61 — Embed access check moved from an in-process cached SiteSetting read to an uncached per-request DB query, adding a round trip to every public /embed/comments and /embed/count hit

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` from checking `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)` (an in-process string/setting check) to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, i.e., a database query, with no caching shown in the diff. Since `ensure_embeddable` runs for embed requests (e.g., `/embed/comments`, `/embed/count`), this introduces a per-request DB round trip where previously there wasn’t one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Unguarded `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError and aborts the migration when no `embed_category` setting row exists.
db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Host values are interpolated into raw INSERT SQL, so a quote in the value aborts the migration mid-upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds an INSERT statement via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If any existing `site_settings` value line `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), the SQL becomes syntactically invalid and the migration can fail mid-upgrade; it also creates an SQL injection surface against the migration runtime. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16 — host.destroy` has no nil guard, so a stale DELETE returns HTTP 500 instead of 404.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy`. If the record doesn’t exist (stale/invalid id), `host` will be nil and `nil.destroy` will raise a NoMethodError, resulting in a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:11 — update` passes a possibly-nil record to `save_host`, returning 500 for a concurrently-deleted host.
app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 — params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is dereferenced without checking the param exists, yielding 500 instead of 400.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without guarding that `params[:embeddable_host]` is present. If a client sends a malformed request (or no body / wrong key), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be `nil`, and `nil[:host]` will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 rather than a controlled 4xx response. This is directly verifiable from the added controller code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil, 500ing before validation can return 422.
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `self.host.sub!` in `EmbeddableHost` raises `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil during the before_validation callback, which is exactly the golden issue (nil `host` causing `sub!` to crash).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:10 — update` persists nothing yet returns 200, so operator changes are silently discarded.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action (line ~10) only calls `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads params or persists anything. The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` was added, and the Ember controller includes an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit this endpoint and receive a successful response despite no state being saved. So any future/attempted updates to embedding-level settings via this endpoint would be silently ignored, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch`, so a failed DELETE surfaces no error to the admin.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` but does not attach a `.catch(...)` handler. By contrast, the save action explicitly does `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the DELETE request fails (network/server validation/permission), the promise rejection is unhandled here and no error is shown to the admin, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197 — obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError if any `*_ids` key is null, aborting hydration of the whole payload.

adjudication.rationale: In the new plural-handling branch of `_hydrateEmbedded` (matching keys like `*_ids`), the code unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)`. If the server payload contains a `*_ids` key whose value is `null`/`undefined` (or otherwise not an array), this will throw a `TypeError` and stop hydration for the entire object. The diff adds this new `*_ids` path and does not include any guard like `Array.isArray(obj[k])` before calling `map`, so the failure mode is real given such input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:201 — The raw `*_ids` key is deleted even when every lookup returned undefined, silently losing the ids.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6, the new plural branch for keys matching /(.+)\_id(s?)$/ always executes `delete obj[k];` after mapping ids through `_lookupSubType`. Even if `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` for every id (e.g., the embedded objects aren’t present in `root`), the original `*_ids` array is removed and replaced with an array of `undefined` values under `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`. Unlike the singular branch (which only deletes when `hydrated` is truthy), this unconditionally drops the raw ids, so the finding is accurate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowers only the column, so mixed-case referers silently fail the allowlist.
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the query lowercases the database column but not the host parameter, causing mixed-case host inputs (e.g., referer hosts) to fail matching despite intended case-insensitive comparison.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — category: eh.try(:category_id)` passes an integer id and nils out on lookup failure, silently misrouting embedded topics.
app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:6 — this.get('embedding').update({})` discards the promise, giving no failure feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In admin-embedding controller, `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` without `.then/.catch` or `return`, so the promise (if `update` returns one) isn’t explicitly handled here. However, the diff does not show any UI invoking `saveChanges` (the new `embedding.hbs` only has `addHost`/`deleteHost` actions), and Discourse/Ember apps often have global AJAX error handling. The claim that this “gives no failure feedback” is therefore not a clearly verifiable defect introduced by this diff (it’s at most a potential improvement/code smell).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lower-cases only the stored DB value, not the incoming `host` argument, so matching correctness for any non-browser caller (e.g. `TopicRetriever`/API-supplied URLs) that isn't already lower-cased silently fails closed instead of being enforced consistently in code

adjudication.rationale: In EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, the lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. This applies `lower()` to the DB column but not to the bound `host` value. Since the model does not downcase `self.host` in `before_validation` (it only strips scheme/path) and `record_for_host` also doesn’t explicitly downcase the extracted hostname, the match can become case-sensitive on the RHS (notably on PostgreSQL) and fail for inputs containing uppercase characters even though hostnames are case-insensitive. The diff provides no guarantee that all callers always pass a lowercased hostname, so this is a real correctness risk in the introduced code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — Only assertion is that the class subclasses Admin::AdminController, so create/update/destroy ship with zero behavioral coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In the added spec `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb`, the only example asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`. There are no tests exercising the controller’s actual behavior (e.g., create/update/destroy responses, authorization, parameter handling, error cases). Given this diff introduces new controller actions with nontrivial logic, the finding that it ships with effectively zero behavioral coverage is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:6 — Tautological superclass assertion means show/update and the new admin routes are never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new spec `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only asserts `Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController`, which is guaranteed by the controller definition (`class Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController`) and does not exercise the `show`/`update` actions or the new `/admin/customize/embedding` routes added in `config/routes.rb`. This is a verifiable gap: the spec provides no coverage for the behavior the diff introduces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:1 — New model ships with no spec file covering its validation regex, normalization, record_for_host or host_allowed?.

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add a spec file for the new model: `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb`. While it doesn’t exhaustively test the validation regex with many invalid cases, the claim that there is “no spec file covering its validation regex, normalization, record_for_host or host_allowed?” is contradicted by the added spec file and its tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196 — New `_ids` plural hydration branch in shared store code is added with no JS test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:13 — "raises an error with a missing host" arranges nothing and now passes only because referer is nil.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the test "raises an error with a missing host" no longer sets up the old SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts (removed in this diff) nor does it set a request referer. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1 — Category and embeddable_host fabricator file contents were swapped, so each file no longer matches its name.
